reason: The original Cursor session did not rebuild after the reported follow-up. The only new Cursor claim used the explicitly excluded second session identifier and created a different workspace; the tester directed that the Cursor path be recorded as failed. This observation does not establish why Cursor routed the follow-up that way.
observations: The initial Cursor and Claude QA builds succeeded and each returned one ephemeral agent_relay_credential in the build-secret metadata endpoint. Cursor mapped it to AGENT_RELAY_CURSOR_TOKEN and Claude to SELF_HOSTED_RUNNER_ENVIRONMENT_SECRET. The tester confirmed normal initial replies. Neither stop build carried a build secret in its metadata.

Only the two recorded QA workspaces were stopped with explicit approval. The tester reported a Cursor follow-up in the original conversation, but the resulting claim carried the excluded second Cursor session identifier, not the original 5:24 session identifier. The original Cursor workspace stayed stopped and never had a start rebuild in this run; the excluded workspace was not touched and later cleaned up naturally.

Claude redelivered the original session identifier and rebuilt the same QA workspace as build 3 at 23:38:12 UTC. Its new build succeeded, the agent connected, and the build-secret metadata endpoint returned a fresh ephemeral agent_relay_credential. The tester confirmed a normal Claude reply later; exact provider reply time is unknown.

No secret values or build-parameter responses were retrieved: the parameter endpoint can include values. Absence of a legacy credential build parameter was therefore not directly verified. The rebuilt Claude and excluded Cursor workspaces exited cleanly and were deleted by Relay. After explicit approval, only the stopped original Cursor workspace was deleted. By 00:05:42 UTC on November 6, no QA template workspace remained and both baseline pools were healthy.
